'''Tong Yang''' ({{langx|zh|杨彤}}) is a Chinese mathematician known for his contributions to the field of partial differential equations and kinetic theory.<ref name="Tong Yang, Google Scholar">{{cite web|title=Tong Yang, Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.com.hk/citations?user=l22eWrkAAAAJ&hl=en}}</ref> He has been serving as a Chair Professor of Mathematical Science in the Department of Applied Mathematics at [[The Hong Kong Polytechnic University]] (PolyU)<ref> {{cite web|title=Tong Yang, Department of Applied Mathematics, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Retrieved January 13, 2025|url=https://www.polyu.edu.hk/ama/people/academic-staff/prof-yang-tong/}}</ref><ref name="HoD of CityU Math">{{cite web|title=Warm Welcome to Chair Professor Yang Tong to the AMA Family, retrieved January 15, 2025|url= https://www.polyu.edu.hk/en/ama/news-and-events/news/2022/warm-welcome-to-our-new-faculty-member-prof-yang-tong/}}</ref> since 2020. Previously, he held the position of President of The Hong Kong Mathematical Society from 2016 to 2020<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.hku.hk/HKMS/ | title=The Hong Kong Mathematical Society - 香港數學學會 }}</ref> in 2016-2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=2016-2018 Council Member, The Hong Kong Mathematical Society |url= https://www.math.hku.hk/HKMS/members2016.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2018-2020 Council Member, The Hong Kong Mathematical Society|url=https://www.math.hku.hk/HKMS/members2018.html}}</ref>

== Education ==
Yang completed his Ph.D. in 1993 at the [[University of California, Davis]] in USA,<ref name="Tong Yang, Mathematics Genealogy Project">{{cite web|title=Tong Yang at the Mathematics Genealogy Project|url= https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=12652}}</ref> after earning his bachelor's and master's degrees from [[Zhongshan University]] in 1987 and 1990,<ref name="Tong YANG, ORCID">{{cite web|title=Tong Yang, ORCID|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9807-7230}}</ref> respectively.

== Research ==
Yang's research focuses on [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]] and [[kinetic theory]].<ref name="Tong Yang, homepage">{{cite web|title=Tong Yang, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Retrieved January 13, 2025|url=https://www.polyu.edu.hk/ama/profile/tongyang/}}</ref> In collaboration with [[Tai-Ping Liu]], he introduced the Liu-Yang functional, which is used to evaluate the stability of BV solutions in systems of hyperbolic [[Conservation law|conservation laws]].<ref name="Liu-Yang functional">{{cite web|title=T.-P. Liu, T. Yang, L1 stability for 2×2 systems of hyperbolic conservation laws, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (3) (1999) 729–774|jstor=2646212 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/pdf/2646212.pdf}}</ref><ref name="Liu-Yang functional 1">{{cite web|title=Liu, T. P., & Yang, T. (1999). L1 stability for systems of hyperbolic conservation laws. Contemporary Mathematics, 238|url=https://www.ams.org/publications/books/monographs/B0-8218-1196-7-03547-7.pdf}}</ref> This work addressed significant challenges in the well-posedness theory for conservation laws and has applications in various fields.<ref name="Liu-Yang functional 3">{{cite web|title=T.-P. Liu, T. Yang, Well-posedness theory for hyperbolic conservation laws, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 52 (12) (1999) 1553–1586|doi= 10.1002/(SICI)1097-0312(199912)52:12<1553::AID-CPA3>3.0.CO;2-S|url= https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/%28SICI%291097-0312%28199912%2952%3A12%3C1553%3A%3AAID-CPA3%3E3.0.CO%3B2-S}}</ref><ref> {{cite book|title=  Advances in the Theory of Shock Waves |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-0193-9_1 |last=Liu |first=Tai-Ping |chapter=Well-Posedness Theory for Hyperbolic Systems of Conservation Laws |date=2001 |series=Progress in Nonlinear Differential Equations and Their Applications |volume=47}}</ref>

Additionally, Yang and his collaborators developed a new macro-micro decomposition for the [[Boltzmann equation]] to study its fluid phenomena,<ref name="Macro-micro">{{cite web|title=Liu , T.P. , Yang , T. , Yu , S.H. ( 2004 ). Energy method for Boltzmann equation. Physica D 188: 178 – 192|doi=10.1016/j.physd.2003.07.011 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167278903003142}}</ref><ref name="Macro-micro cited">{{cite book|title=Saint-Raymond, L. (2009). Hydrodynamic limits of the Boltzmann equation (No. 1971). Springer Science & Business Media| isbn=978-3-540-92846-1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ROUILXXb7UUC&pg=PA13 | last1=Saint-Raymond | first1=Laure | date=26 March 2009 | publisher=Springer }}</ref> facilitating the application of analytical techniques used in conservation laws.

== Awards ==
Yang has been recognized as one of the World's Top 2% most-cited scientists by [[Stanford University]] from 2020 to 2024.<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Ioannidis | first1=John P. A. | last2=Baas | first2=Jeroen | last3=Klavans | first3=Richard | last4=Boyack | first4=Kevin W. |title=A standardized citation metrics author database annotated for scientific field| journal=PLOS Biology | date=2019 | volume=17 | issue=8 | article-number=e3000384 | doi=10.1371/journal.pbio.3000384 | doi-access=free | pmc=6699798 }}</ref> He received the [[Morningside Medal|Morningside Silver Medal of Mathematics]] "for his contributions to the well-posedness theory for hyperbolic conservation laws".<ref name="Morningside Medalist"></ref> In 2011/12, he was awarded The Croucher Senior Research Fellowship for his work on mathematical theories related to the Boltzmann equation <ref name="Croucher SRF 2011"></ref> He also received the second-class award of 2012 [[State Natural Science Award]] in China for his project on "conversation laws and the Boltzmann equation"<ref name="2012 State Award Cert"></ref><ref name="2012 State Award"></ref>

In 2019, Yang earned the first-class award in Natural Sciences of the Higher Education Outstanding Scientific Research Output Award (Science and Technology) by [[Ministry of Education (China)|the Ministry of Education of China]] for his joint work on well-posedness of the Prandtl equation in Sobolev spaces.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexandre, R., Wang, Y. G., Xu, C. J., & Yang, T. (2015). Well-posedness of the Prandtl equation in Sobolev spaces. Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 28(3), 745-784|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/jams/2015-28-03/S0894-0347-2014-00813-4/S0894-0347-2014-00813-4.pdf}}</ref><ref name="1st MoE 2019"></ref><ref name="MoE first prize cert 2019"> {{cite web|title= 2019 MoE Higher Education Outstanding Scientific Research Output Award - First Prize|url=https://www.polyu.edu.hk/ama/profile/tongyang/MoE_First%20prize_2019.pdf}}</ref> He received another first-class award in 2022 <ref name="MoE Higher Education Outstanding Scientific Research Output Awards"></ref><ref name="ASHK Newsletter"></ref> for his work on mathematical theory of compressible Navier-Stokes equations and related models.<ref>{{cite web|title= Vong, S. W., Yang, T., & Zhu, C. (2003). Compressible Navier–Stokes equations with degenerate viscosity coefficient and vacuum (II). Journal of Differential Equations, 192(2), 475-501|doi= 10.1016/S0022-0396(03)00060-3|url= https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022039603000603}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Li | first1 = Hai-Liang
 | last2 = Li | first2 = Jing
 | last3 = Xin | first3 = Zhouping
 | arxiv = 0811.3818
 | doi = 10.1007/s00220-008-0495-4 | doi-access = free
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Communications in Mathematical Physics
 | mr = 2410901
 | pages = 401–444
 | title = Vanishing of vacuum states and blow-up phenomena of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations
 | volume = 281
 | year = 2008}}</ref> In 2020/2021, he was awarded the RGC Senior Research Fellowship by the [[University Grants Committee (Hong Kong)|University Grants Committee]] for his project "Some Mathematical Theories for Kinetic Systems".<ref name="RGC SRF"></ref><ref name="RGC Award Presentation Ceremony (2020/21)"></ref>

Yang has been elected to various prestigious memberships and fellowships. In 2018, he became a Foreign Fellow of the European Academy of Sciences for his contributions to science and technology.<ref name="EAS Foreign Member 2018 Cert"> {{cite web|title= Foreign Member, European Academy of Sciences 2018|url=https://www.polyu.edu.hk/ama/profile/tongyang/EAS%20Foreign%20member%202018.pdf}}</ref> He was named a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for his work on hyperbolic conservation laws and kinetic equations.<ref name="AMS Fellow"></ref><ref name ="Class of 2021 Fellows of AMS">{{cite web|title=Fellows of AMS 2021, Notices of the American Mathematical Society, pp 642, Vol 68, No.4, April 2021, retrieved January 20, 2025|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202104/202104FullIssue.pdf?adat=April%202021&trk=&cat=none&type=.pdf}}</ref> In 2021, he was elected as a member of the World Academy of Sciences for his fundamental contributions to hyperbolic conservation laws, kinetic theories, boundary layer theories, and high [[Reynolds number]] limit.<ref name="TWAS Fellow"></ref><ref name="CityU Scholars"></ref> He became a member of Academia Europaea in 2022<ref name="AE member 2022"></ref><ref name="AE member 2022_1"></ref>
